rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This problem-solving plan starts by connecting the known power rule to the new product rule through one complete example. Short sessions then move from guided use to independent retrieval, application, and error repair. Each session fits a 15-minute availability window and keeps one main action prominent.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Build the product rule procedure and see why both terms are necessary.
sessions.amountLabel: The rule and one complete worked derivative
contentTargets: Interpret and apply d/dx[f(x)g(x)] = f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x) in one worked example
completionEvidence: Explain what changes and what stays unchanged in each term of the product rule
Apply the rule to reproduce the worked derivative with labeled factors

sessions.title: Use the Rule With Guidance
sessions.objective: Differentiate a product by following the procedure one step at a time.
sessions.amountLabel: One guided polynomial product and one similar attempt
contentTargets: Differentiate a product of two polynomial expressions before simplifying
completionEvidence: Solve one guided product-rule derivative with both required terms
Solve one similar derivative with prompts removed

sessions.title: Choose and Apply the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Recognize product-rule problems and solve them without a displayed formula.
sessions.amountLabel: One classification check and two independent derivatives
contentTargets: Distinguish products requiring the product rule from expressions handled directly by the power rule
completionEvidence: Classify several expressions by the differentiation rule they require
Solve two product-rule derivatives without procedural prompts

sessions.title: Verify Independent Use
sessions.objective: Demonstrate accurate product-rule use and repair any remaining error.
sessions.amountLabel: Two mixed problems and one error correction
contentTargets: Identify and correct a missing-term or differentiation error
completionEvidence: Solve two mixed derivative problems and justify the chosen rule
Correct a flawed product-rule solution and explain the error

coverage.focus: Interpret and apply the product rule in one worked example.
essentialIdeas: Differentiate a product by applying the product rule: differentiate the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the differentiated second.
completionEvidence: The learner states the product rule in their own words.
The learner identifies which factor is differentiated in each term.
The learner produces the correct derivative for a product example.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study one accurate example of the product rule, explain it in your own words, repair any gap, and explain it again.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining the relationship helps reveal missing parts and build a usable mental model before independent work.
how: Study the example and notice what changes in each term.
State the rule in plain language.
Compare your explanation with the model and fix any missing piece.
Explain it again without copying the wording.
methodBriefing.completion: You can state the rule accurately, name what changes in each term, and apply it to a product example.
personalization: Keep one visible step at a time.
Treat the final explanation as a fresh restatement, not a copy.

activities.label: Product rule example
activities.title: One product-rule example
activities.body: Review the example and notice what changes in each term.

essentialIdeas: Differentiate a product by applying the product rule: differentiate the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the differentiated second.

activities.label: Say the rule back
activities.title: Put it in your own words
activities.body: Answer from memory in one or two sentences.
activities.concept: Apply the product rule to one worked example
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate the first factor times the second, then add the first factor times the derivative of the second factor.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms and shows that one factor is differentiated while the other stays the same in each term.

activities.label: Fix the missing term
activities.title: Correct the rule pattern
activities.body: Revise your answer if anything was missing.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Leaving out one of the two terms in the product rule
activities.concept: Apply the product rule to one worked example
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the derivative of the second factor.
activities.feedback: If one term was missing, the fix is to include both parts of the product rule. One factor changes at a time, while the other stays in place.

activities.label: Explain it again
activities.title: Explain the rule again
activities.body: Give a fresh explanation in plain language.
activities.concept: Apply the product rule to one worked example
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate one factor while keeping the other factor unchanged, then switch and do the same for the other factor, and add the two results.
activities.feedback: A strong response says what stays the same and what changes in each term, not just the formula.

check.title: Apply the product rule
check.prompt: Differentiate h(x)=x^2sin x using the product rule.
check.referenceAnswer: h'(x)=2x sin x + x^2 cos x.
